summary.en: In **reported speech** we tell someone else's words from a later point of view. After a past reporting verb (_said_, _told_, _asked_) the tense usually moves back (**backshift**), and pronouns, places and time words change: _"I'll call you tomorrow."_ → _She said she would call me the next day._ Questions keep statement order, and orders or requests use **tell/ask + object + to-infinitive**.
summary.es: Es el «dijo que…» del español, pero en inglés la concordancia de tiempos es más rígida: «Dijo que vendrá» suele ser **said she would come**. Recuerda que **say** no lleva complemento de persona directo (said to me) y **tell** sí (told me).

form: Backshift: present simple → past simple; present continuous → past continuous; present perfect/past simple → past perfect
will → would; can → could; may → might; must → had to
Time and place: _today_ → _that day_; _tomorrow_ → _the next day_; _here_ → _there_; _now_ → _then_
Questions: **asked + if/whether/question word + subject + verb** (no do/does/did)
Orders and requests: **told/asked + object + (not) to + infinitive**
Reporting verbs: _admit, deny, suggest, promise, warn, insist_ have their own patterns

uses.text: **Questions**: _"Where do you live?"_ → _He asked me where I lived._
**Orders and requests**: _"Don't be late."_ → _She told us not to be late._
**No backshift needed** when the fact is still true or the reporting verb is present: _He said he lives in Oslo_ (he still does). _She says she's tired._

note.en: Backshift is optional when the reported information is still true or has just been said.
note.es: El retroceso de tiempos es opcional si lo dicho sigue siendo cierto.

uses.text: **Reporting verbs with other patterns**: _She admitted taking the money. He suggested meeting earlier. They warned us not to go._

mistakes.wrong: She said me that she was busy.
mistakes.right: She told me that she was busy.

why.en: Tell needs a person object. Say does not: she said that… or she said to me that…
why.es: Told me / said (to me): say no lleva complemento de persona directo.

mistakes.wrong: He asked me where did I work.
mistakes.right: He asked me where I worked.

why.en: Reported questions use statement order, with no did.
why.es: En la pregunta indirecta no se usa did ni inversión.

mistakes.wrong: She asked me if I can help her.
mistakes.right: She asked me if I could help her.

why.en: After a past reporting verb, can usually becomes could.
why.es: Tras un verbo en pasado, can pasa a could.

mistakes.wrong: The doctor told me to not smoke.
mistakes.right: The doctor told me not to smoke.

why.en: Negative reported orders use not to + infinitive.
why.es: El orden normal es not to + infinitivo.

mistakes.wrong: He suggested me to take a taxi.
mistakes.right: He suggested that I take a taxi.

why.en: Suggest is not followed by object + to-infinitive. Use a that-clause or -ing.
why.es: Suggest no admite objeto + to + infinitivo: that I take / taking.

examples.en: "I'm meeting a client at noon," she said. → She said she was meeting a client at noon.
examples.es: Dijo que se reunía con un cliente a mediodía.

examples.en: He told me he had lost his wallet on the way home.
examples.es: Me dijo que había perdido la cartera de camino a casa.

examples.en: The receptionist asked whether we had a reservation.
examples.es: La recepcionista preguntó si teníamos reserva.

examples.en: She told the children to put their coats on.
They asked me not to share the document with anyone.
He said he'd finish the work by the following Friday.
I asked her what time the exhibition opened.
The driver warned us that the road might be icy.
She admitted that she hadn't read the contract.

practice.prompt: "I'll send the files tonight," she said. → She said she ___ the files that night.

explanation.en: After said, will usually becomes would.

practice.prompt: "Where do you work?" he asked me. → He asked me where I ___.

explanation.en: Reported questions use statement order and the backshifted tense, with no did.

practice.prompt: "Don't open the window," said Mum. → Mum told me ___ the window.

explanation.en: A negative reported order uses not to + infinitive.

practice.prompt: She ___ me that the flight had been cancelled.

explanation.en: Tell takes a person object (me); say does not.
